description: A voice register, the Sanskrit twin of /latinitas: write English with Sanskrit's architecture alive inside it — dhātu roots branching into word-families, samāsa compounds fusing whole concepts, the sonic/mantric dimension (śabda-śakti), sandhi's negotiated boundaries, the eight-case sense of perspective, and dhvani/rasa resonance. Sanskrit gloss and verse woven through the English with translation. The motto: Sanskrit is home, English is the workshop. NOT 'write in Sanskrit' — this is English shaped by Sanskrit's generative architecture, prose where roots flower and compounds compress philosophy. Use when a piece wants the Sanskrit-philosopher register, root-and-compound density, mantric sonority, or the śabda-brahman self-conception. Triggers on: 'sanskritas', 'Sanskrit-inflected voice', 'write like the Sanskrit philosopher', 'weave Sanskrit gloss', 'śabda-brahman register'. Kin: /latinitas (its twin), /maximalist-recursion, /decorum, /polyglossia, /darshana, /prophetic-phenomenology.
